findings.issue_text: Permission check in addGuests.handler.ts uses `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` instead of `||`, denying team admins who are not owners and making the admin path unreachable

BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS comparison is case-sensitive against a lowercased list because incoming guest emails are not lowercased, allowing blacklist bypass with mixed-case emails like Blocked@Example.com

EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the requesting user's credentials) instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong or empty credential set and external calendar/video events are silently not updated
Duplicate emails within the submitted `guests` array are not deduplicated server-side, so a direct tRPC call with repeated addresses creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany
Existing-attendee dedup compares `guest === attendee.email` case-sensitively, so adding Foo@Bar.com when foo@bar.com already exists creates a duplicate attendee and duplicate invite

`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so filtered-out (already-attendee or blacklisted) emails receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification
organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without a guard, throwing on bookings with no attendees and failing the entire email send

`guests` in addGuests.schema.ts has no maximum array length and the handler has no rate limiting, allowing a single request to inject hundreds of attendees and trigger mass outbound emails (email amplification abuse vector)
Booking is fetched without a `status` filter, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings and sending scheduled/ICS REQUEST emails for a dead event
No seat-capacity check for events with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, so appending guests as attendees can exceed the seat limit

Read (findFirst for existing attendees) and write (booking.update + createMany) are not in a transaction and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent add-guest requests with the same email both insert
In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `message` is always a non-empty template string, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and exposing raw error codes to users
MultiEmail.tsx keys removable list items by array index, causing React DOM reuse and focus/uncontrolled-input glitches when removing a middle email
ZAddGuestsInputSchema is constructed on every render inside the AddGuestsDialog component body and its `.refine` has no error message; it should be hoisted to module scope with a refinement message
No tests accompany the new addGuests handler — permission branches (isOrganizer/isAttendee/team admin), blacklist filtering, and dedup paths are uncovered

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the requesting user's credentials) instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong or empty credential set and external calendar/video events are silently not updated

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`), but it builds `EventManager` with credentials from the requesting user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`. When the requester is an attendee or a team admin/owner (not `booking.userId`), this credential set can be different from (or empty compared to) the booking organizer’s credentials. Yet `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is invoked to update external calendar attendees for the booking. From the diff alone, there is no switch to use `booking.user.credentials` (which were included in the booking query) or the organizer’s credentials, so the external update can run with the wrong credentials in those valid code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicate emails within the submitted `guests` array are not deduplicated server-side, so a direct tRPC call with repeated addresses creates duplicate attendee rows via createMany
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying issue: the server filters existing/blacklisted guests but does not deduplicate repeated emails within the incoming guests list, allowing createMany to insert duplicate attendee rows when the client submits duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Existing-attendee dedup compares `guest === attendee.email` case-sensitively, so adding Foo@Bar.com when foo@bar.com already exists creates a duplicate attendee and duplicate invite

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, existing-attendee deduplication uses a strict, case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since neither `guest` nor `attendee.email` is normalized (e.g., to lowercase) anywhere in this diff (schema just validates `.email()`), inputs like `Foo@Bar.com` will not match an existing attendee stored as `foo@bar.com`, allowing a duplicate attendee record to be created via `attendees.createMany`. This can also lead to duplicate calendar/email notifications for what is effectively the same email address.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so filtered-out (already-attendee or blacklisted) emails receive a full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the add-guests notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering `guests` to exclude already-attendees and blacklisted emails, and only `uniqueGuests` are actually persisted via `createMany`. However the code later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the unfiltered raw input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, attendee email handling is based on `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` to decide whether to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the caller includes an email that was already an attendee (and thus filtered out of `uniqueGuests`), that existing attendee will still be present in `calendarEvent.attendees` and will match `newGuests.includes(...)`, causing them to receive the wrong email type. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts accesses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without a guard, throwing on bookings with no attendees and failing the entire email send

adjudication.rationale: While `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts` does access `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name` without an explicit guard, the new call path introduced in this diff (`addGuestsHandler` -> `sendAddGuestsEmails`) constructs `evt.attendees` from `bookingAttendees.attendees` after a `createMany` that only runs when `uniqueGuests.length > 0` (otherwise it throws). Therefore, in the newly added functionality, `calEvent.attendees` should be non-empty (at least the newly added guests), so the alleged “bookings with no attendees” case is not verifiably reachable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `guests` in addGuests.schema.ts has no maximum array length and the handler has no rate limiting, allowing a single request to inject hundreds of attendees and trigger mass outbound emails (email amplification abuse vector)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authed TRPC mutation `viewer.bookings.addGuests` whose input schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the request body is used to `createMany` new attendees and then triggers outbound email sending via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` and sends emails (plus organizer/team member emails) in a `Promise.all`. There is no per-request cap or throttling in this handler, so an authenticated caller with permission can submit a very large `guests` array and cause large DB writes and mass outbound emails in a single request (amplification/abuse/DoS vector).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking is fetched without a `status` filter, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings and sending scheduled/ICS REQUEST emails for a dead event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched solely by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and then updated to create new attendees and trigger calendar updates + `sendAddGuestsEmails(...)`. There is no check or filter on any booking lifecycle field (e.g., `status`) before allowing the mutation. As written, any booking record that exists and passes the permission checks (organizer/attendee/team admin/owner) can have guests added and will send ICS/REQUEST emails via the new email flow, regardless of whether the booking is cancelled/rejected/otherwise inactive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No seat-capacity check for events with `seatsPerTimeSlot`, so appending guests as attendees can exceed the seat limit

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new records to `booking.attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and then updates calendar attendees/emails, but it never checks `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (which is loaded and later placed onto the `CalendarEvent` as `seatsPerTimeSlot`). Since seat-limited events use attendee count as capacity, this mutation can add arbitrary additional attendees after the booking exists, potentially exceeding the seat limit. There is also no guard in the UI action to prevent this for seat-based events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Read (findFirst for existing attendees) and write (booking.update + createMany) are not in a transaction and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so concurrent add-guest requests with the same email both insert

adjudication.rationale: The handler does a non-transactional read of existing attendees (`prisma.booking.findFirst(... include: { attendees: true })`), computes `uniqueGuests` in memory, then performs a separate write (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`). That means concurrent requests can both see the same pre-state and attempt to insert the same guest email(s). However, the finding’s claim that “there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email)” is not verifiable from this diff (no Prisma schema/migration is shown). If such a constraint exists, the second insert would fail rather than create duplicates. So the concurrency risk is real, but the proposed finding as stated (asserting no unique constraint and definite duplicate insertion) is not strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, `message` is always a non-empty template string, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and exposing raw error codes to users

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the error handler builds `message` using a template literal: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;`. A template literal always produces a string, even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (it becomes the text "undefined") and even if the translation is empty, so `message` will still be truthy (e.g., "undefined: "). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never use the fallback, making it dead code. The constructed message also directly includes `err.data?.code` (a raw TRPC error code like `BAD_REQUEST`, `FORBIDDEN`), which will be shown to users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx keys removable list items by array index, causing React DOM reuse and focus/uncontrolled-input glitches when removing a middle email

adjudication.rationale: In packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx the list renders `value.map((field, index) => (<li key={index}> ... ))`. Items can be removed via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. Using the array index as the React key means keys for all subsequent items change after a middle deletion, so React may reuse DOM nodes for different emails, which commonly manifests as input focus/cursor jumping or the wrong input retaining state. This is a real defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ZAddGuestsInputSchema is constructed on every render inside the AddGuestsDialog component body and its `.refine` has no error message; it should be hoisted to module scope with a refinement message

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is indeed created inside the component and thus recreated on each render, and the `.refine(...)` call does not provide a custom error message. However, in this diff that does not cause a verifiable bug/correctness issue: the code only checks `safeParse(...).success` and then sets a local `isInvalidEmail` flag to show a fixed translation key (`emails_must_be_unique_valid`). It never reads or displays Zod’s refinement error message. Recreating the schema per render is at most a minor performance/style nit, not a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests accompany the new addGuests handler — permission branches (isOrganizer/isAttendee/team admin), blacklist filtering, and dedup paths are uncovered

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality (addGuests handler, dialog, UI component), but it does not include any test files or test changes. However, the proposed finding goes beyond what’s verifiable: it asserts specific branches/paths are “uncovered,” which cannot be confirmed from the diff alone (there could be existing tests elsewhere, and branch coverage is not shown). Also, “no tests accompany” is a process/quality suggestion rather than a concrete defect introduced by the code itself.
